Before Bloodhound Q50 Was Killed, Vlad Tried To Convince Him to Leave Chicago (Flashback)
recentItems.description: In this flashback, we revisit Bloodhound Q50’s appearance on VladTV, where DJ Vlad praised the late rapper’s career and encouraged him to consider leaving his hometown of Chicago. Known for his thoughtful approach to interviews, Q50 discussed navigating the media spotlight while avoiding unnecessary controversies. Vlad emphasized the importance of focusing on music rather than feuds, pointing to Chief Keef as an example of an artist who relocated to distance himself from conflict. Q50 acknowledged the advice, explaining that as his career continued to grow, he was gaining new experiences that could expand the stories he shared through his music beyond Chicago. Vlad also highlighted the dangers rappers can face in their hometowns, sharing examples of artists who experienced tragic violence. He ultimately urged Q50 to consider relocating for his safety, longevity, and future in the music industry.

recentItems.title: TK Kirkland on Boosie Paying $600K for Trump Pardon: He Needs to Charge It To the Game (Part 1)
recentItems.description:
Become a VladStocks Member now: https://www.youtube.com/vladtv/join
---------
T.K. Kirkland returns to VladTV to react to Boosie’s 60 Minutes interview about allegedly losing $600,000 while trying to secure a Donald Trump presidential pardon. Speaking with Vlad, Kirkland says the situation proves “anybody can get got” and advises people to “put a face to the money” before doing major business through consultants or third parties.  

Vlad breaks down claims involving Republican consultants, disputed text messages, and reports that Boosie may never have filed an official pardon application. The conversation also touches on attorney Bradford Cohen, who helped Lil Wayne and Kodak Black receive Trump pardons, plus online debate over whether the case could raise bribery concerns. Kirkland argues Boosie is a victim and says the loss may simply be something he has to charge to the game—possibly even discuss with an accountant as a business expense.

Trap Lore Ross: The Feds' Biggest Claim Was Lil Durk Facetime'd Killers After the Hit (Part 3)

Part 1: https://youtu.be/fgzkOWzO-eY
--------
Trap Lore Ross joins Vlad to break down the Lil Durk/OTF trial, the jury’s verdict, and why he believes the government’s evidence still raised serious questions despite falling short beyond a reasonable doubt. Ross points to the feds’ late closing-argument claim that Durk was allegedly on FaceTime with the men in the BMW after the shooting, asking about shots fired and what happened. He and Vlad also discuss cell-site evidence, Jam and Vonnie’s testimony, the alleged car switch, guns and hoodies being ditched, In-N-Out, San Diego return flights, and Durk’s manager Jason allegedly booking travel during the chaos.

The conversation also covers the October 24, 2024 FBI raids on OTF members, why Jason was not arrested, speculation around potential witnesses, and names raised in court and online, including Doody Lo, Buni Mo, Brick Baby, India, Rolling 60s rumors, and Reddit theories.

recentItems.title: Mario Sanchez on Being Locked Up with Erik Menendez After He Killed His Parents (Part 7)
recentItems.description:

Part 6: https://youtu.be/IXyVE6t29Ds
Part 1: https://youtu.be/-pWadYhoSkc
--------
Mario Sanchez speaks with Vlad about his time in prison alongside Erik Menendez, recalling how he crossed paths with him on the non-active side of New Folsom roughly 30 years ago. The conversation revisits renewed public interest in Erik and Lyle Menendez following recent documentaries, dramatizations, and social media debate over whether the Menendez brothers could be released.

Sanchez weighs in on the upcoming parole hearing, California’s shifting approach to long-term prisoners, and the broader reality of inmates with murder convictions receiving second chances after decades behind bars. He also shares his perspective on the long-running debate surrounding the Beverly Hills case: whether the brothers acted after alleged abuse by their father or were privileged young men motivated by money.

This clip offers a firsthand prison-era perspective on Erik Menendez, the Menendez brothers case, New Folsom, California parole laws, and one of America’s most discussed true crime stories.

recentItems.title: Max B: I Lied About Sleeping with Jim Jones' Girl Chrissy on "Touched It In Miami" (Part 8)
recentItems.description:

Part 7: https://youtu.be/H37S-nTXqGI
Part 1: https://youtu.be/FoBBj-6j544
--------
Max B sits down with VladTV to revisit one of the most discussed chapters in his Dipset-era fallout with Jim Jones. Reflecting on “Touched It in Miami,” Max admits he falsely claimed he slept with Chrissy, saying the line was meant to get under Jim’s skin during a tense period when he felt blocked from making money or getting radio play. He also talks about having a 75-year sentence hanging over him at the time and how that affected his mindset.

The Harlem rapper breaks down street encounters involving Jim Jones, a car incident, and the escalating atmosphere around their beef. Max also addresses the Public Domain 3 mixtape controversy, including Juelz Santana’s name appearing on a tombstone cover he says he didn’t approve, explaining the real cover was inspired by Milli Vanilli. A candid look at hip hop conflict, Dipset history, and rumors finally being cleared up.

Chingy sits down with VladTV to address St. Louis media personality 607 Unc and his controversial claim that he wrote some of Nelly’s biggest hits. The “Right Thurr” rapper shuts the allegation down, calling it attention-seeking while offering a nuanced take on 607’s online persona, trolling, and viral commentary. Chingy also reacts to talk that he was the only artist to “defeat” Nelly, referencing past diss records and the attention economy driving hip-hop debates online.

The conversation also covers Chingy’s new single “Gold Chain Confessions,” his upcoming project and sound, “Luxury Midwestern Soul,” and the lasting impact of classics like “Holiday,” “Pullin Me Back,” “One Call Away,” and “Right Thurr.” Vlad and Chingy discuss St. Louis slang, Drake and Fredo Bang showing respect, Charlamagne Tha God, VladTV’s role in resolving conflicts, and broader hip-hop stories involving Terrance “Gangsta” Williams, Lil Diesel, Charleston White, Mob James, Diddy, and Tupac.

Part 1: https://youtu.be/K7__iCx2ghE
--------
Attorney Bradford Cohen joins Vlad to break down how he represented Drake during the XXXTentacion murder trial controversy, when a defense lawyer attempted to subpoena the Toronto rapper over an unsupported theory that Drake had paid for a hit. Cohen explains why the subpoena attempts failed, how the judge viewed the claims as irrelevant, and why Drake was never required to testify in the Florida case involving XXXTentacion’s killing.

Cohen also discusses another civil subpoena matter involving Drake, his brief work connected to Ice Spice after the viral McDonald’s altercation, and his philosophy on using lawsuits to deter future harassment or assaults. The conversation expands into celebrity legal strategy, civil litigation costs, Megan Thee Stallion’s defamation battle with a blogger, and why public figures often take aggressive legal action even when financial recovery is unlikely. A candid look at hip-hop, law, media narratives, and courtroom tactics.

recentItems.title: Nicholas Irving Calls the Afghanistan Exit a Pure Political Debacle (Part 6)
recentItems.description:
Become a VladStocks Member now: https://www.youtube.com/vladtv/join

Part 5: https://youtu.be/09wmzBfleFk
Part 1: https://youtu.be/4D3wB1ZOXlA
--------

Combat veteran Nicholas Irving sits down with Shawn Prez for a blunt discussion on how politics shapes war — and the deadly cost for troops on the ground. Irving says shifting rules of engagement under George W. Bush, Barack Obama, and Joe Biden often left service members “fighting with their hands behind their backs,” especially in Afghanistan. He breaks down why the U.S. withdrawal under Biden became, in his view, both a political and military debacle, pointing to the loss of more than a dozen service members, the Taliban’s rapid return to power, and the collapse of 20 years of American nation-building. The conversation also touches on Vietnam comparisons, the Tet Offensive, taxpayer funding, midterm politics, oil prices, Iran, and the tension between public pressure to bring troops home and the need for a sound military strategy. Watch the full interview for Irving’s unfiltered perspective.
